I want to know! Did you use AI during the L.A. wildfires?

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/d…

Columbia Journalism Review (@CJR)

The LA Fires and what a disaster says about our physical and informational environments, by @Jon_Allsop. cjr.org/the_media_today/la_w…




— https://nitter.net/CJR/status/1878829345621659711#m

Matt Pearce 🦅🇺🇸 (@mattdpearce)

TAX ZUCKERBERG, FUND KICK-ASS LOCAL JOURNALISTS 

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/c…



— https://nitter.net/mattdpearce/status/1878607938547585212#m

TAX ZUCKERBERG, FUND KICK-ASS LOCAL JOURNALISTS 

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/c…
Those who mark students’ work already know a particularly pronounced version of this, I think.

Strong feeling that uni lecturers are the canary in this particular coal mine. The best thing* about marking work is getting enthusiastic about students' enthusiasm. But we can't do that anymore; we have to constantly suspicious. It stinks.

According to my termination letter from @washingtonpost.com a, the company cited these two Bluesky posts, and claimed that I disparaged white men, accused me of ‘gross misconduct’, and that my Bluesky posts “potentially endanger[ed] the physical safety of our staff”.
This quote is spot on
Rob I hope your ears were burning, you were subconsciously somewhere in the back of my head when I was pondering all this.

"AI" means no more good-faith assumptions of a writer's investment and attention on the basis of their text; it imposes a collective and metastasizing burden of paranoia on everyone  
mattdpearce.substack.com/p/ai-imposes...

too much computer 

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/ai-imposes...

cf. Matt Pearce: "Artificial intelligence is an anti-community technology whose principal civic innovation is to reduce social trust and engender a greater sense of unreality in our lives."

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/ai-imposes...
you gotta see how Michael Douglas eats a bagel in Fatal Attraction
“It’s an earnest embrace of AI’s surreality that is in some ways more challenging to cope with than the lying, because at least a liar knows they’re doing something wrong.”

Sunday blog: AI is making us paranoid.

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/ai-imposes...
news outlets should put politicians’ screen time in parentheses after their name on first reference

There are lots of things that have gone wrong for the news media in the 21st century, but the feature they have in common is the destruction of incentives to produce accurate information. 

www.niemanlab.org/2026/05/you-...
“Adjusted for inflation, hourly wages are up 3% since the end of 2019 while profits are up 50%.”

The thing everybody needs to understand in 2026 is that upmarket journalism is an Hermès factory. It’s expensive and labor-intensive and a little stuffy because that’s what the audience is. The second you introduce open-plan office thinking into a medieval process is when the clientele smells CHEAP

imho the Byron Allen swap-out for Colbert is one of those MBA-brain profit-maximizing schemes that might actually work on a pure accountancy level, but the 60 Minutes stuff is just screaming Disruptor Delusion
